collection: NERDC JSS 1 Digital Technologies online safety and privacy
note: Original classroom practice using fictional scenarios. Independent academic review pending.

questions.subject: Digital Technologies
questions.learningObjective: Explain what HTTPS protects and why the site address still matters.
questions.prompt: A practice browser shows a secure connection, but its address is different from the school portal address printed on a teacher’s handout. What does the secure connection protect? What should the pupil do before entering a password?
questions.answer: HTTPS protects data in transit to the displayed site. Open the address from the trusted school handout and check that it matches the intended portal before signing in.
questions.explanation: Connection encryption protects the exchange with the site shown in the browser. The actual address helps a pupil check whether it is the intended site.

markingGuide.description: Explains protection of data in transit.
Uses the known school address to verify the intended site before entering credentials.

questions.subject: Digital Technologies
questions.learningObjective: Interpret a connection warning and protect sensitive information.
questions.prompt: A pupil opens a familiar school portal on a shared tablet, but the browser warns that the connection cannot be verified. A classmate suggests continuing because the page looks familiar. Explain what the pupil should do and why.
questions.answer: Stop before entering details and ask a teacher or school technician to check the warning. The page design does not establish that the connection is trustworthy.
questions.explanation: A connection warning means the browser could not verify protection as expected. A pupil can wait for the school to check the issue.

markingGuide.description: Avoids entering details or bypassing the warning.
Explains why appearance is insufficient and seeks appropriate help.

questions.subject: Digital Technologies
questions.learningObjective: Apply a safe browsing rule to a download decision.
questions.prompt: A club’s teacher has provided a link to a practice worksheet. While looking for it, a pupil sees a pop-up asking them to install a tool first. Explain how to obtain the worksheet safely and what to do with the unexpected pop-up.
questions.answer: Dismiss the pop-up without accepting its request. Open the teacher’s known resource directly and ask the teacher if the worksheet cannot be accessed there.
questions.explanation: Using the approved source avoids installing unrelated software simply because a pop-up asks for it.

markingGuide.description: Uses the teacher-provided source or verifies the requirement with the teacher.

questions.subject: Digital Technologies
questions.learningObjective: Make a safer choice when an optional permission does not match an activity.
questions.prompt: A practice drawing site asks for permission to access the tablet’s microphone. The planned activity is to upload a picture with no sound. What choice should the pupil make, and what could they check if the site refuses to continue?
questions.answer: Decline microphone access for the drawing task. If blocked, check the site’s explanation or ask the teacher for an approved alternative.
questions.explanation: An app permission should make sense for the task. The exercise provides no reason to record sound.

markingGuide.description: Suggests checking the reason or asking for an alternative.

questions.subject: Digital Technologies
questions.learningObjective: Create practical online safety commitments with a reporting step.
questions.prompt: Write a three-line pledge for pupils using shared school tablets. Include one rule before downloading, one rule for handling personal information and one action if a browser shows a warning.
questions.answer: Use only teacher-approved downloads. Keep personal details out of public forms and posts. Stop and tell a teacher if the browser warns that a connection cannot be verified.
questions.explanation: A pledge is useful when each commitment describes an action a pupil can take.

markingGuide.description: Includes a specific rule protecting personal details.
Includes a workable action in response to a warning.

questions.subject: Digital Technologies
questions.subtopic: Deciding which details a form needs
questions.learningObjective: Explain the privacy benefit of sharing only information relevant to an activity.
questions.prompt: A fictional club artwork form needs the title of a drawing and the artist’s class code. An optional field asks for the artist’s home address. Explain which details are enough and one privacy benefit of leaving the address blank.
questions.answer: Provide the artwork title and class code. Leaving the home address blank reduces how much personal information the form operator keeps or might later share.
questions.explanation: Sharing fewer unrelated details reduces exposure if a record is copied, shared or mishandled.

markingGuide.description: Explains a concrete privacy benefit of omitting the address.

questions.subject: Digital Technologies
questions.learningObjective: Choose a new password after compromise and explain why it should be unique.
questions.prompt: A pupil discovers that someone saw the password for a classroom practice account. What change should the pupil make through the official account settings with teacher help? Explain why reusing a password from another account is a poor choice.
questions.answer: Replace the exposed password with a long, unique password through the official settings. Reuse could put another account at risk if the same password becomes known.
questions.explanation: An exposed password should be replaced. A unique replacement limits the effect of exposure across accounts.

markingGuide.description: Replaces the exposed password using the official account route.
Chooses a long, unique replacement and explains the risk of reuse.

questions.subject: Digital Technologies
questions.subtopic: Reviewing who can see a link
questions.learningObjective: Choose audience settings that limit access to a classroom submission.
questions.prompt: A pupil must share a presentation with the teacher. The sharing menu offers “Anyone with the link” and “Only people added”. Choose a setting, explain how to give the teacher access, and say what the pupil should check before submitting.
questions.answer: Choose Only people added and add the teacher’s school account as a viewer. Check that the correct account is listed and the presentation is still restricted to intended people.
questions.explanation: Restricted sharing lets the intended person read the file without granting access to everyone who obtains the link.

markingGuide.description: Adds the teacher with suitable viewing permission.
Checks the intended audience or access list.
